node: SCORE_MAX in js/online.js equals the cap in firestore.rules (5,000,000)
node: the name pattern in firestore.rules is the one the client uses (1 to 12 chars, ASCII letters, digits, space . _ -)
node: client name test: aliases and plain names pass; empty, 13 chars, leading space or hyphen, accents, HTML, quotes and blocklisted words (any case, embedded) fail
node: whole-token blocklist: Kumar, Kumari, Shitote, Shitanda, Himalaya, Mbooni, Kunyanga, Malayan, Scunthorpe and Pissarides are ALLOWED
node: every blocklist word is DENIED alone, in upper case, with digits around it (6word9), as a separate token (a word, word.x, x_word, 1-word) and with s, es, er, ing
node: enabled() is false under file:// even with a full config, false with an empty config, true only for http: or https: with projectId and apiKey
node: under file:// top, flush, submit and queue make zero XHR calls and store nothing
node: queue keeps ONE pending record and the higher score (a lower or equal one is ignored, a higher one replaces it)
node: rename updates the pending name only (empty or missing record: no change)
node: only a score above onlineBest is queued; 0, negative, NaN, text and above-cap scores never are
node: corrupt stored pending, auth and onlineBest read as empty and do not throw

sim: two tabs on shared storage: B (900) flushed right after A (500) sent waits for the window (nothing at 0 s or 5 s), then sends exactly once; the server holds 900, B's pending record is gone, nothing is lost
sim: a "too soon" 403 KEEPS the pending record (900), counts attempts = 1 and does not touch onlineBest
sim: the retry waits 11 s after the answer (nothing at +6 s), then first re-reads the server copy (one GET) and sends once; the 900 lands and the record is cleared
sim: slow answer: a follow-up 11.1 s after the request left (8.1 s after the answer) is NOT sent; it goes out 11 s after the answer and the server accepts it (no 403)
sim: a 403 that never goes away: attempts 1, 2, 3 are 11 s or more apart (nothing at +10 s), the record is dropped after the third, and nothing more is sent ever after
sim: 429 keeps the record with attempts 1; 400 drops it at once with no retry; a 500 keeps it with no retry loop
sim: after a 403 the retry re-reads the server copy: same score and same name clears the record without sending (onlineBest resynced); same score but another name is a rename and is sent
sim: a record cleared by another tab while this tab waited is not sent (the pending record is re-read after the wait); queue keeps the higher score
sim: before sending the client checks what the rules check: a score below onlineBest is dropped unsent, a blocklisted name falls back to the alias, a bad name with a bad alias is dropped unsent
sim: the send time is stored in shared storage (matatuRush.lastSend) from the injected clock, stamped at the request and again at the answer

sim: clock a year ahead for a send, then corrected: the stored time is repaired, the next flush sends after exactly one window (nothing at 10.9 s, sent by 11.1 s), is not stuck busy, and the flush after it works too

sim: clock set back a year in the middle of a wait: the wait is NOT repeated, the request goes out when the one window is over (11.1 s after the flush started), the pending record is cleared and no timer is left running
sim: clock a year in the past for a send, then corrected: the stored time is a year old, so the next flush sends at once (no wait, no timer) and the server holds the new score
sim: five more flush calls during a wait all answer "busy", do not push the send later (it still goes out 11.05 s after the first call), and do not send twice

sim: watchdog: a flush whose request never answers is "busy" at 30 s (no second send), a new flush may start after 45 s and sends, the late answer of the dead one does no harm, and flushing is never stuck

sim: refresh answered 400 or 403: one fresh sign-up (exactly one /v1/token call and one signUp), the new id is stored and used in the commit, the record is sent; refresh answered 500: no sign-up, record kept
sim: after a refresh 403 the stored anonymous id is a NEW id (not the old one) and the commit is written under it
sim: own-entry read fails (HTTP 500 or 403) with a record at attempts 1: the send still goes out in the same flush and is cleared when accepted (never stuck unsent)

sim: a failed read counts as an attempt: read fail + refused send from attempts 1 reaches 3 and drops the record after ONE send; attempts 2 + failed read drops it unsent; a read with no answer is not counted and the send goes ahead
